name: MDEA
addictionPotential: Moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
toxicities: Pharmacology, metabolism and toxicity data for MDEA are almost nonexistent. As a serotonin releaser, excessive doses may cause serotonin syndrome, potentially fatal if untreated.
effectsSummary: MDEA is closely related to MDMA. It differs mainly in how well one's own feelings are perceived (entactogenic effect), how strong empathic understanding (empathic effect) and hallucinogenic effects occur.
dosageRemark: The archived oral table lists threshold 40 mg, light 70-120 mg, moderate 120-180 mg, strong 180-225 mg, heavy 225 mg+; total 3-6 h, onset 20-60 min, comeup 15-30 min, peak 1.5-2 h, offset 1-2 h, afterglow 12-48 h. Educational user/resource compilation, not a recommendation. The page says pharmacology, metabolism and toxicity data are almost nonexistent; lightMin corrected from threshold to source light lower bound. The page gives a weight-based guide: 1.3 mg per kg body weight (1.3 mg x 80 kg = 100 mg, up to 1.3 mg x 100 kg = 130 mg).
generalRisks: The page describes MDEA as potentially habit-forming and urges caution and harm reduction. Sustained temperature elevation and serotonin syndrome risk at excessive doses.
longtermRisks: Pharmacology, metabolism and toxicity data are almost nonexistent and identifies MDEA as potentially habit-forming.
saferUse: Caution and harm reduction are urged, because MDEA may be habit-forming and there is almost no data on its pharmacology, metabolism or toxicity.
The page warns excessive doses may cause serotonin syndrome and sustained body-temperature elevation, and advises one to three months between uses.
summary: A quite rare empathogen closely related to MDMA. Yet is less potent than the prior.
